focus: D1 Correctness - check-script logic and doc-stated thresholds against the code

findingDetails.title: A user flow is never held to the 12-connector budget the shared rule states
findingDetails.evidence: BUDGET sets USER_FLOW: (9, None) and the comparison at flowchart.py:236 treats None as no connector cap; references/flow-mode.md:298 states the general budget of 9 nodes and 12 connectors applies unless the type sets its own, and references/types/user-flow.md:66 sets only the node count.
findingDetails.recommendation: Set the user-flow budget to (9, 12) in the BUDGET table, or record the intended cap in references/types/user-flow.md:66.
findingDetails.scopeProof: flowchart.py:47 is the only budget table; flowchart.py:236-240 is the only budget comparison; no other module reads BUDGET.

findingDetails.title: The first declared node is excused from the way-in rule whatever its shape
findingDetails.evidence: first_id is steps[0].id (flowchart.py:233) and exempts any shape at flowchart.py:155, while references/types/user-flow.md:59 says only a stadium starts or ends the flow.
findingDetails.recommendation: Exempt a start only when its shape is a stadium; ENDPOINT_SHAPES already covers the loop-back case.
findingDetails.scopeProof: flowchart.py:233 sets first_id from declaration order and flowchart.py:155 is its only consumer.

findingDetails.title: An arrow table in the sequence check is defined and never read
findingDetails.evidence: ARROWS maps the four accepted arrows to their meanings and no line in the file reads it; the arrow decision uses REFUSED_ARROWS at sequence.py:83 and the MESSAGE pattern at sequence.py:33.
findingDetails.recommendation: Delete the table, or use it where an arrow is classified.
findingDetails.scopeProof: grepped the packet for ARROWS; outside its definition the only hits are REFUSED_ARROWS, and no module imports the name.

findingDetails.title: The state check accepts TD while its message and type reference allow LR or TB
findingDetails.evidence: DIRECTIONS = {LR, TB, TD} at state.py:21 while state.py:46 and references/types/state.md:60 say LR or TB; mermaid_extract.py:101 defaults an undeclared state diagram to TD, so an undeclared direction passes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Drop TD or fold it into TB as flowchart.direction_family does, and align state.py:46 with references/types/state.md:60.
findingDetails.scopeProof: state.py:21 and state.py:45-46 are the whole direction rule for the state profile; state.md:60 is the stated rule. Doubt stated: TD and TB are one Mermaid direction, so the acceptance may be deliberate and only the wording stale.

spec_code.notes: process, architecture, sequence and state budgets match the code; the user-flow connector budget does not

checklist_evidence.notes: quality-rubric.md:88 defers the layout budgets to layout.py; no checklist.md in the packet
